name: Westfield Sheet Metal Products, LLC
old_description: Westfield Sheet Metal Works, Inc., located in Kenilworth, New Jersey, has been in existence since 1928 as a union shop affiliated with Sheet Metal Workers Union Local 22. Our 50,000 square foot manufacturing and office facility, located on a 100,000 square foot lot, is equipped to service your metal fabrication needs from design to installation.
about:
Westfield Sheet Metal Works, Inc. has operated in Kenilworth, New Jersey since 1928 as a union shop affiliated with Sheet Metal Workers Union Local 22. The company occupies a 50,000-square-foot manufacturing and office facility on a 100,000-square-foot lot at North 8th Street and Monroe Avenue.

The shop provides custom metal fabrication from design through installation, handling projects that range from small machine guards to 10-by-10-foot plenums requiring crane lifts. In-house capabilities include engineering and project management, shearing, bending, welding, polishing, painting, quality control, and delivery, all coordinated from CAD drawings or sketches.

The firm serves architectural, commercial, construction, and manufacturing clients. Completed projects include the Streicker Bridge, light pylons for Gantry Plaza, structural elements for Hunters Point South Park, Madison Square Garden, and Hunts Point Landing. A historic-restoration contractor also cites Westfield for stainless-steel and copper components on landmark buildings.

Westfield emphasizes full-project control under one roof, with a union workforce guiding each job from initial sketch to final installation, and highlights on-time, on-budget delivery as a core differentiator.

name: Westmoreland Plastics Co
old_description: is a well-established custom manufacturer of quality thermoset and thermoplastic molded components. For over fifty years we have supplied a wide variety of industries with critical parts and sub-assemblies. Our superior customer service, attention to detail, and a willingness to try new and innovative processing methods have allowed us to remain successful in a demanding and very competitive market place.
about:
Westmoreland Plastics Co operates from Latrobe, Pennsylvania, where it has produced custom thermoset and thermoplastic molded components for more than fifty years. The privately held company began as a molding operation and has since added engineering, tooling, and precision finishing capabilities.

The shop specializes in thermoset and thermoplastic molding, offering tooling design and construction as well as the ability to run customer-supplied molds. Value-added services include lapping and fine grinding, and the company maintains an ISO-certified quality system to verify that each component meets specification. Production scales from prototype runs to higher-volume orders, though specific annual volumes are not disclosed.

Its parts serve aerospace, appliance, electrical distribution, lighting, medical and metering, sensor, and temperature-control markets, with applications ranging from circuit breakers to medical devices. Customers include original equipment manufacturers seeking reliable, specification-compliant plastic components.

Westmoreland Plastics emphasizes responsive customer service, attention to detail, and a willingness to adopt innovative processing methods as the reasons it has remained competitive in a demanding marketplace. The company also cites its ISO certification and in-house lapping and grinding as differentiators that reduce lead times and ensure dimensional accuracy.

name: Westshore Electronics
old_description: Westshore has been providing innovative engineered solutions since 2003. Our broad experience in electronic and mechanical design, coupled with software development, has allowed us to grow with our customers. Simply bring us your ideas and we’ll assist with your product from concept through production.
about:
Westshore Electronics was founded in 2003 in Holland, Michigan. The company began as an engineering-focused firm providing electronic and mechanical design alongside software development.

The company operates as a contract electronics manufacturer offering a full range of services from concept through production. Its capabilities include double-sided surface-mount assembly, flexible and metal-core PCB assembly, through-hole and mixed-technology assembly, automated selective wave soldering, fine-pitch component placement down to 01005 packages, BGA placement, conformal coating, microcontroller programming, and 100% functional testing. The facility also handles cable assemblies, electromechanical box builds, and finished-goods assembly.

Westshore serves small and mid-tier manufacturers in the medical, industrial controls, durable goods, and inspection lighting sectors. Customers typically require embedded control systems, high-density circuit boards, LED PCBAs, instrument lighting, and electromechanical controls.

The company emphasizes a single-source partnership model, combining design, manufacturing, component sourcing, and supply-chain management under one roof. Its quality system is built around an ISO 9001:2015-certified QMS that includes on-site IPC training, a track-trace-control system, first-article approval, and risk-mitigation tools such as PFMEA, PPAP, and 8D analysis.

name: Whaling City Solar
old_description: Whaling City Solar is a residential and small-commercial solar installation company based in New Bedford, MA. We serve customers throughout the South Coast and Cape Cod. The company was founded in 2020 to create a better customer experience when purchasing solar equipment. We see many door-knocking, cold calling, and social media ad companies showing one picture of solar, while in reality, solar systems can take dozens of forms. We founded our company to tailor fit each and every array to its home and owners.
about:
Whaling City Solar is a residential and small-commercial solar installation company based in New Bedford, Massachusetts. Founded in 2020, the company was started to create a better customer experience for purchasing solar equipment, moving away from high-pressure sales tactics toward tailored system design for each home and owner.

The company designs and installs photovoltaic systems for homes and small businesses across southeastern Massachusetts and Cape Cod. Its five-step process covers site assessment and financial analysis, in-house permitting and interconnection management (including Eversource and municipal approvals), single-day installation by crews split between roof-mounted racking and electrical work, post-installation inspections, and system commissioning with monitoring portal access. The team includes engineers, project managers, foremen, and a master electrician; specific hardware deployed includes REC, Solaria, and QCell modules, Enphase IQ8+ microinverters or SolarEdge string inverters, and Enphase Encharge, FranklinWH, or SPAN battery storage.

Whaling City Solar serves residential homeowners and small commercial property owners in communities such as Mattapoisett, New Bedford, and Westport. The company emphasizes local presence—its staff live and work in the service area, giving them familiarity with regional weather, electrical inspectors, and lending institutions.

The founders aimed to replace door-knocking and cold-call sales with transparent, straightforward service: no sales commissions, no call centers, quotes delivered within 24 hours of a site visit, and all permitting handled internally. They position themselves as a local alternative that tailors each array to the specific property and owner.

name: White Sands Woodworks Inc.
old_description: Karl is such an exceptional gentlemen. We are so thankful to have come across his business. Karl provides quality work and attention to detail. Being able to find someone who specializes in wood work was important, but finding someone who is extremely passionate about what he does was the icing on the cake. If you’re looking for someone to depend on to make your vision come true and you enjoy a positive environment, Karl is your guy.
about:
White Sands Woodworks operates from Alamogordo, New Mexico, where it was established in 2014 by Karl Peter. A family‑owned business, it traces its roots to Peter’s childhood in Germany restoring antique furniture alongside his father. After nearly three decades of service in the German Air Force, Peter retired and opened the shop near Holloman Air Force Base, drawing on the surrounding White Sands landscape for inspiration and name.

The company produces custom wood and metal pieces through a blend of traditional hand craftsmanship and modern tooling. Core processes include fine woodworking, blacksmithing and forging, laser engraving, epoxy resin casting, furniture and cabinetry construction, knife making, and precision cutting of materials such as acrylic. Output ranges from cutting boards, picture frames, and quarter‑map displays to tables, chairs, shelves, cabinets, steak turners, custom blades, and military‑themed gifts such as challenge‑coin displays, flag cases, and shadow boxes. No facility size or headcount figures are published.

Customers span military personnel seeking personalized retirement or PCS gifts, homeowners commissioning furniture and décor, businesses ordering custom pieces, and individuals looking for one‑of‑a‑kind presents. Reviews cite projects for a 1:250 million scale model of Neptune’s rings, restoration of a century‑old oak table, and rapid turnaround on plaques for award ceremonies.

Peter states the shop was founded to carry forward a German tradition of meticulous craftsmanship while integrating contemporary technology. The brand emphasizes a fusion of old‑world artistry — honed through years of antique restoration — with state‑of‑the‑art equipment to deliver tailored, heirloom‑quality work.

name: Whitesburg Electronics Inc
old_description: Founded by Wayne Jacks in 1977, Whitesburg Electronics. manufactures high-quality electronics and electro-mechanical assemblies and provides solutions for government, industry, and commercial clients.
about:
Whitesburg Electronics Inc was founded in 1977 by Wayne Jacks in Lacey's Spring, Alabama. The company remains family-owned, with Jacks serving as owner and CEO and his daughter June B. Jacks as vice president.

The company manufactures printed circuit board assemblies, wiring harnesses, cable assemblies, and full electro-mechanical assemblies from a 32,500-square-foot facility equipped with Juki surface-mount placement machines. Its capabilities span through-hole and fine-pitch SMT (down to 5 mm), manual and machine high-reliability soldering, conformal coating, potting, chassis wiring, and high-volume packaging. Whitesburg handles production runs from medium to large scale, supported by a workforce with over 500 collective years of experience.

Whitesburg serves government, industrial, and commercial clients. Its customer base includes Fortune 500 firms such as IBM, Caterpillar, Teledyne Brown Engineering, and Boeing, as well as federal agencies like NASA and the Department of Defense, alongside smaller businesses with specialized requirements.

The company emphasizes zero-defect delivery on schedule, backed by a quality system that includes MIL-STD-45208 inspection, ISO/IEC 17025 calibration, IPC-J-STD-001 and IPC-A-610 soldering and assembly standards, and a CFC-free, EPA-compliant cleaning process. Whitesburg also highlights its ability to handle confidential customer requirements and military specifications.

name: WhyGen Solar
old_description: Founded in 2020 during the global pandemic, WhyGen Solar was built to empower sales professionals in the solar industry. CEO Aaron Rice saw a critical gap—most companies focus on profits, not their sales force.
about:
WhyGen Solar is headquartered in Rio Rancho, New Mexico, with additional offices in Tempe, Arizona, and Westminster, Colorado. The company was founded in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic by CEO Aaron Rice, who adopted the "Start With Why" philosophy to create a business centered on empowering sales professionals in the solar industry.

The firm provides solar energy solutions for both residential and commercial customers across the Southwest. Its service portfolio includes outright system purchases, solar loans, and lease or power-purchase agreements, each backed by warranties covering parts, labor, and in some cases production. Installations are performed at homes and businesses in New Mexico, Arizona, and Colorado.

WhyGen Solar serves homeowners seeking to reduce utility bills and businesses aiming to power operations with clean energy. The company markets directly to end users in the residential and commercial segments, offering consultation, financing coordination, and installation management.

The founding premise was that when sales representatives thrive, customers win. Rice built the organization around training, support, and an experience-focused culture for its sales force, a differentiator he identified as missing in a market he viewed as overly profit-driven.

name: Wicked Grain Custom Furniture
old_description: All of our items are made to last and we stand by our work! We support local farmers and mill workers right here in the Midwest and ALL of our items are 100% made in the US! We can do a wide range of styles and types of furniture pieces, but all of our items have a rustic or natural feel to them. We love using organic shaped slabs, pieces of wood with cool grains/knots/character marks, and wood that has a story.
about:
Wicked Grain Custom Furniture operates from Overland Park, Kansas. The company traces its origins to 1916, though details about its founding family or early history are not publicly documented. It specializes in slab and reclaimed wood furniture with a rustic, natural aesthetic.

The shop produces custom furniture from scratch, including live-edge tables, slab furniture, barn doors, vanities, and accessories. Each piece is one-of-a-kind, crafted from organic-shaped slabs featuring distinctive grains, knots, and character marks. The company does not carry pre-made inventory; every item is built to order using wood sourced from local Midwest farmers and mills. Finishing includes food-safe oils for items such as cutting boards.

The customer base appears to be primarily residential, as reflected in testimonials from homeowners who commissioned custom dining tables, vanities, and barn doors. The company also serves clients seeking rustic industrial or farmhouse-style pieces, such as the "Farmhouse Leaf Table" and "The Santa Fe" industrial live-edge slab table.

Wicked Grain emphasizes that all products are 100% made in the United States and that it supports local farmers and mill workers. The company says its differentiation lies in using wood with a story—organic slabs with natural character—and in standing behind its work with a commitment to heirloom quality.

name: Wil-Clair Sheet Metal
old_description: In 1999, Wil-Clair was founded by John Svetlecic, as he brought along two of his former employees, David Ogle and Allen Kubicki, with him. David was in charge of the financial side of the business, while Allen served as the head of the shop. To this day, both of them still serve as John’s right-hand men. While the right pieces were certainly in place, the business wasn’t an overnight sensation. The first year saw revenue around $100,000, but it wasn’t long till the growth started and continued for years to come. To put into comparison the leaps made over these past two decades, 2016 saw sales at nearly four and a half million. Over this time period, the employee count has rose leaps and bounds, along with plenty of expansions to the main office and warehouse space.
about:
Wil-Clair Sheet Metal was founded in 1999 in Kansas City, Missouri, by John Svetlecic after he left a co-owned sheet metal shop following a strategic disagreement. He brought two former colleagues—David Ogle, who handled finances, and Allen Kubicki, who ran the shop floor—and both remain with the company today.

The shop specializes in custom sheet metal fabrication, offering fiber laser cutting, five-axis waterjet cutting (on an Omax Maxiem 1530), certified welding, metal rolling, press brake forming, plasma cutting, complex bending, tile cutting, and custom metal sign production. Work ranges from prototypes to production runs, supported by modern equipment and a team that includes veterans with 20-plus years at the company.

Customers span food processing (equipment platforms for Kellogg’s and Tyson), consumer goods (signage for Procter & Gamble), plumbing and mechanical contracting (Stine-Nichols Plumbing), entertainment (Worlds of Fun), and design-build construction firms (Impact Fabrication, CDI). The company also serves general industrial sheet metal needs.

Wil-Clair differentiates itself through a self-described “Blacksmith Sheet Metal methodology” centered on problem-solving: “We’ll do whatever it takes to get the job done for our clients,” says CEO Svetlecic, whether that means high-tech software or hand-drawn layouts. Clients also note direct access to leadership—CEO, shop superintendent, or foreman—and a commitment to equal attention on every job.

name: Wild Mile Woodworks
old_description: Since 1998, Wild Mile Woodworks has offered timber frame home construction from its Bigfork shop in Northwest Montana. Shop-built timberframe projects have been installed on the grid and off the grid in locations across Montana, Wyoming, Washington, British Columbia and Alberta. Wild Mile Woodworks offers new home design and construction, and timberframe construction, as well as historic structure renovation. Notable
about:
Wild Mile Woodworks was founded in 1998 in Bigfork, Montana, a small community in the state's northwest corner. The company began as a timber frame shop serving the local region and has since expanded its reach across multiple states and into Canada.

The shop provides a full range of timber frame services, including design, milling, joinery, and on-site installation. Projects are built in the Bigfork facility and then erected on location, whether on the grid or off the grid. The company has completed work in Montana, Wyoming, Washington, British Columbia, and Alberta. A notable project is the restoration of the historic Glacier Park Lodge in East Glacier.

Wild Mile Woodworks serves residential clients seeking custom timber frame homes as well as commercial and institutional customers needing historic structure renovation. The portfolio includes traditional chalet-style frames, modern designs, and rustic recycled-wood projects. The Glacier Park Lodge restoration demonstrates capability in large-scale historic preservation.

The company emphasizes a blend of traditional, old-world craftsmanship with modern design techniques. This approach, combined with in-house design and fabrication, allows them to control quality from raw timber to finished structure.
